name: Pat Garrett
life: “I still remember writing a diary through six house moves.” On Wednesday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Pat checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I kept a diary nobody read for sixty years. I would like to enter mine under my own steam.
appearance: Pat has salt-and-pepper curls, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cream pullover. It usually goes with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. When somebody else has the floor, Pat rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Pat uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Pat well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To submit a diary by personal choice.
family: Graham Jackson is Pat’s cousin. Pat is free to hang up first. Graham makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Rent in a biscuit tin*, Graham says, “The handwriting on my envelope is my late wife's.”
connections: Iva Hayes. An older diarist and a translator compare what genuinely consenting to publication feels like.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the manuscript returned unopened
reactions.response: Pat returns the pages privately without treating keeping them closed as a verdict on the work.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Pat brings the envelope to the counter unopened and stays long enough to make a note of who accepted it.
